title: Getting Started with curveRcore
text: Neither curveRfreq curveRbayes preprocess data. transforms must applied upstream via curveRcore::preprocess_standards(). clean separation ensures fitting engines receive data identical scale, making results directly comparable. preprocess_standards() applies four steps order: compute_concentration() — converts dilution column absolute concentration using undiluted standard concentration; optionally log₁₀-transforms result. correct_prozone() — dampens hook effect high concentrations compressing post-peak signal toward peak. perform_blank_operation() — applies one five blank strategies: "ignored" (default), "included" (append geometric mean extra point), "subtracted", "subtracted_3x", "subtracted_10x". compute_log_response() — applies log10() response. Values ≤ 0 floored 1 % minimum positive value among included points transformation. Key contract: preprocess_standards(), column named independent_variable holds log₁₀ concentration response column holds log₁₀ response. scales fitting engines expect.
code: std_raw   <- bead_assay_example$standards blank_raw <- bead_assay_example$blanks  # Preprocess one curve at a time, then stack std_preprocessed <- do.call(rbind, lapply(   split(std_raw, std_raw$curve_id),   function(df) {     cid              <- df$curve_id[1]     blanks_for_curve <- blank_raw[blank_raw$curve_id == cid, ]     result <- preprocess_standards(       data                 = df,       antigen_settings     = list(standard_curve_concentration = 30),       response_variable    = "mfi",       independent_variable = "concentration",       is_log_response      = TRUE,       blank_data           = blanks_for_curve,       blank_option         = "subtracted",       is_log_independent   = TRUE,       apply_prozone        = TRUE     )     result$data   } ))  # Both columns are now on the log10 scale head(std_preprocessed[, c("curve_id", "concentration", "mfi")]) #>     curve_id concentration      mfi #> 1.1        1   -1.52287875 1.964654 #> 1.2        1   -1.04575749 2.476663 #> 1.3        1   -0.52287875 3.047580 #> 1.4        1   -0.04575749 3.616883 #> 1.5        1    0.47712125 4.094851 #> 1.6        1    0.95424251 4.276834

title: Model Forms: Mathematics of the Five curveRcore Calibration Models
text: five models share following parameter convention, enforced across entire curveR ecosystem: independent variable xx scale-agnostic: monotone transformation (e.g. x=log⁡10(concentration)x = \log_{10}(\text{concentration})) applied upstream R model called. models perform transformation internally, except loglogistic4 loglogistic5, require x>0x > 0 raw (un-logged) concentration scale.

title: Model Forms: Mathematics of the Five curveRcore Calibration Models
text: y=+d−a1+exp⁡(−x−cb) y = + \frac{d - }{1 + \exp\!\left(-\dfrac{x - c}{b}\right)} \tag{4PL} 4PL symmetric inflection point (c,(+d)/2)(c,\,(+d)/2). workhorse model log-linear immunoassay standard curves.
code: # Parameter set used throughout this vignette p4 <- list(a = 100, b = 0.8, c = 1.5, d = 50000)  x_seq <- seq(-1, 4, length.out = 300) y_4pl <- logistic4(x_seq, p4$a, p4$b, p4$c, p4$d)  plot(x_seq, y_4pl, type = "l", lwd = 2, col = "#2166AC",      xlab = expression(log[10](concentration)),      ylab = "Response (MFI)",      main = "4PL forward curve") abline(v = p4$c, h = (p4$a + p4$d) / 2, lty = 2, col = "grey50") legend("topleft", legend = "logistic4", lwd = 2, col = "#2166AC", bty = "n")

title: Model Forms: Mathematics of the Five curveRcore Calibration Models
text: y=+d−(1+exp(−x−cb))g y = + \frac{d - }{\left(1 + \exp\!\left(-\dfrac{x - c}{b}\right)\right)^{g}} \tag{5PL} g=1g = 1 reduces exactly 4PL. g>1g > 1 compresses lower shoulder (skews toward upper asymptote); 0<g<10 < g < 1 compresses upper shoulder. inflection point shifts gg: xinf=c+bln⁡(g),yinf=+(d−)(gg+1)g x_{\inf} = c + b\ln(g), \qquad y_{\inf} = + (d-)\left(\frac{g}{g+1}\right)^{g}
code: p5 <- list(a = 100, b = 0.8, c = 1.5, d = 50000, g = 0.6)  y_5pl <- logistic5(x_seq, p5$a, p5$b, p5$c, p5$d, p5$g)  plot(x_seq, y_4pl, type = "l", lwd = 2, col = "#2166AC", lty = 2,      xlab = expression(log[10](concentration)),      ylab = "Response (MFI)",      main = "4PL vs 5PL (g = 0.6)") lines(x_seq, y_5pl, lwd = 2, col = "#D6604D") legend("topleft",        legend = c("logistic4 (g = 1)", "logistic5 (g = 0.6)"),        lwd = 2, col = c("#2166AC", "#D6604D"), lty = c(2, 1), bty = "n")

title: Model Forms: Mathematics of the Five curveRcore Calibration Models
text: y=+d−a1+(c/x)b y = + \frac{d - }{1 + (c / x)^{b}} \tag{LL4} c>0c > 0 EC50 raw concentration scale, bb Hill coefficient. classical Hill equation / dose-response parameterisation. Domain restriction: requires x>0x > 0. working log⁡10\log_{10} scale, logistic4 algebraically equivalent preferred.
code: p_ll4 <- list(a = 100, b = 1.8, c = 30, d = 50000)  # c is EC50 in AU/mL x_conc <- seq(0.01, 500, length.out = 500)  y_ll4 <- loglogistic4(x_conc, p_ll4$a, p_ll4$b, p_ll4$c, p_ll4$d)  plot(log10(x_conc), y_ll4, type = "l", lwd = 2, col = "#4DAC26",      xlab = expression(log[10](concentration)),      ylab = "Response (MFI)",      main = "Log-logistic 4PL — concentration scale") abline(v = log10(p_ll4$c), lty = 2, col = "grey50")

title: Model Forms: Mathematics of the Five curveRcore Calibration Models
text: y=+(d−)(1+gexp⁡(−b(x−c)))−1/g y = + (d - )\,\bigl(1 + g\,\exp(-b(x - c))\bigr)^{-1/g} \tag{LL5} Richards / generalised logistic curve (Richards 1959). Despite name loglogistic5, xx log-transformed concentration (.e. model operates log scale). g→0g \0 formula approaches Gompertz; g=1g = 1 matches 4PL parameter rescaling.
code: p_ll5 <- list(a = 100, b = 1.2, c = 1.5, d = 50000, g = 0.5)  y_ll5 <- loglogistic5(x_seq, p_ll5$a, p_ll5$b, p_ll5$c, p_ll5$d, p_ll5$g)  plot(x_seq, y_ll5, type = "l", lwd = 2, col = "#762A83",      xlab = expression(log[10](concentration)),      ylab = "Response",      main = "loglogistic5 (Richards / generalised logistic)")

title: Model Forms: Mathematics of the Five curveRcore Calibration Models
text: y=+(d−)exp⁡(−exp⁡(−b(x−c))) y = + (d - )\,\exp\!\bigl(-\exp(-b(x - c))\bigr) \tag{G4} Gompertz intrinsically asymmetric: rises steeply lower asymptote approaches upper asymptote gradually (Gompertz 1825). inflection occurs x=cx = c, yinf=+(d−)/ey_{\inf} = + (d-)/e.
code: p_g4 <- list(a = 100, b = 1.2, c = 1.5, d = 50000)  y_g4 <- gompertz4(x_seq, p_g4$a, p_g4$b, p_g4$c, p_g4$d)  plot(x_seq, y_4pl,  type = "l", lwd = 2, col = "#2166AC", lty = 2,      xlab = expression(log[10](concentration)),      ylab = "Response",      main = "4PL vs Gompertz — asymmetry comparison") lines(x_seq, y_g4, lwd = 2, col = "#BF812D") abline(v = p_g4$c, lty = 3, col = "grey60") legend("topleft",        legend = c("logistic4 (symmetric)", "gompertz4 (asymmetric)"),        lwd = 2, col = c("#2166AC", "#BF812D"), lty = c(2, 1), bty = "n")

text: five models parameterised consistently: = lower asymptote, d = upper asymptote, b = scale/slope (always > 0), c = inflection point, g = asymmetry (5-parameter models ). monotonically increasing scale-agnostic — x argument accepts whatever fitting engine passes (typically log₁₀-concentration).
